title: Deferred-retry failsafe and customer fast-lane for escalated Hosted API traffic
creator: Priya Nair
description: Several recent customer escalations show repeated client retries + long tail timeouts causing amplified 5xx waves and impacting other tenants. This ticket implements two coordinated mitigations: (1) a deferred-retry failsafe that converts repeated/replay retries into a single safe fast-fail or idempotent fallback after configurable windows; and (2) a per-customer 'fast-lane' admission path for escalated customers that isolates their traffic to a bounded worker pool with conservative batching and a short-circuit optimistic fallback. The goal is to stop retry-amplification, preserve SLOs for non-escalated tenants, and provide a reproducible, auditable path to surface errors to support engineers and customer success.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed deferred-retry failsafe to edge proxies and gateway: requests with >N retries within T seconds are transformed to a single hedged request or idempotent fallback
Per-customer fast-lane routing is configurable via Console and respects tenant ACLs; default disabled for non-escalated customers
5xx amplification metric (retry-amplification-ratio) drops by >=50% in the staged test tenant cluster during synthetic replay
No measurable regression in p50/p95 latency for non-fast-lane tenants after rollout
Runbook updated and on-call can enable/disable fast-lane and adjust N/T without a code deploy
implementation_notes: Edge proxy: add lightweight admission shim that tags requests with escalation=true when Console flag present for tenant
Gateway: implement deferred-retry window state (short in-memory token) keyed by idempotency-key or fingerprint, TTL configurable

Behavior: on detection of retry amplification, first action is to convert duplicate concurrent requests to a single hedged request; subsequent duplicates within window get immediate 429-with-retry-after or fast fallback depending on operation idempotency
Runtime: fast-lane worker pool isolated (bounded goroutines + separate connection pool) to avoid head-of-line blocking on shared hosts
Metrics: add retry-amplification-ratio, fast-lane-utilization, deferred-retry-drop-rate; expose per-tenant via Console
Rollbacks: feature gates + traffic-shaping flags; immediate kill-switch that disables fast-lane via central flag and falls back to preexisting admission path
test_plan: Unit tests for admission shim, deferred-retry token lifecycle, and fallback rules
Integration tests: synthetic replay harness to replay production traces with high retry rates against a staging cluster
Load test: scale fast-lane worker pool to worst-case tenant burst and validate isolation of other tenants
Chaos test: kill a fast-lane worker mid-request to validate graceful failover and idempotent fallback
Canary: enable fast-lane for a single non-critical internal tenant and monitor metrics for 24h
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): deploy code and enable deferred-retry failsafe in staging; run synthetic replay for 6h
Phase 1 (canary): enable per-customer fast-lane for internal tenant 'redwood-test-1' for 24h and observe metrics
Phase 2 (limited-prod): enable on up to 5 escalated customer tenants with increased telemetry and on-call readiness
Phase 3 (ramp): if stable, enable Console toggle for SREs and CS to self-serve fast-lane; default keep disabled for all others
Emergency rollback: flip Console 'fast_lane_enabled' to false and revert deferred-retry gating via central flag
monitoring_and_metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for fast-lane vs normal path
alerts: page SRE if retry-amplification-ratio > 0.25 for >10 minutes or fast-lane saturation > 85%
